newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says W Bank unrest will cause Arab casualties.
newsitem.headline: Israel says W Bank unrest will cause Arab casualties.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai warned the Palestinian Authority on Sunday that unrest in the West Bank and Gaza Strip will lead to casualties mainly on the Palestinian side.

While touring the volatile West Bank town of Hebron -- which was quiet on Sunday after eight days of Arab-Israeli clashes -- Mordechai said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was not doing enough to stem the violence.

"I hope that the Palestinian Authority and other forces in the area will use their influence to prevent unnecessary confrontations which will cause casualties mainly on the Palestinian side," Mordechai said.

Israeli soldiers firing rubber bullets wounded scores of Palestinians hurling stones and firebombs in a week of clashes on the confrontation line between Israeli- and PLO-run sectors of the divided city.
"Unfortunately, the Palestinian Authority is not doing what it has to do...to stop all the violence and terrorism in the area of Hebron," he said.

Palestinian police refrained from intervening in the Hebron clashes during most of the week. PLO officials have said the Authority was not ready to enter into a conflict with its people while Israel is expanding Jewish settlements in the West Bank, Gaza and Arab East Jerusalem.
The defence chief dismissed charges the Palestinian Authority was organising the unrest: "the things aren't exactly organised. The scope was relatively limited."
Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to the PLO in January under a peace deal but kept troops to guard fortified enclaves where 400 Jewish settlers live in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs.
